To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
trade liberalization has negative impact on both absolute and relative wage in a small open economy.
trade liberalization reduces both absolute and relative wages of both skilled and un-skilled workers in an open economy comprising of both formal and informal sectors.
trade liberalization has negative impact on both types of workers and it reduces the disparity between the wages of skilled and unskill workers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a theoretical model of a simple open economy comprising of two sectors producing two types of goods, viz, importables and exportables, and a skilled intermediate input.
the impact of trade policy on the relative wages of skilled and unskkled labour in a small open economy.
the impact of trade policy on the distribution of wages.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
tariff reduction leads to a fall in the wage rate of both types of labour, but the fall in the relative wage rate of skilled labour is greater than that of unskilled labour.
the impact of trade on the wage distribution depends on the structure of the economy and the nature of trade.
the impact of trade policy on the wage structure of the developing economy depends on the structure of the economy, factor intensity and the relative factor endowments of the country.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
trade liberalization reduces wage disparity between skilled labour and unskilled one.
trade liberalization leads to reduction of wage disparity between skilled workers and unskilled ones.

the present paper is a modest attempt to study the impact on wage distribution under trade liberalization when skilled intermediate input is used in import competing sector and the wage structure is not determined by the factor price equalization theorem.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of intermediate input in the production process can be used to explain the wage inequality in the developing countries.
trade liberalization may reduce the wage disparity between skilled & unskilled workers in a developing economy.
in a small open economy trade liberalization may reduce wage disparity between skilled & unskilled workers.
